subject: Medihub – volume ladder, platform fee phasing & SLA carve-outs
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Klein <sara.k@medihub.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 09 Oct 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Medihub – volume ladder, platform fee phasing & SLA carve-outs

Hi Sara —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our conversation I sketched a pragmatic packaging approach that tries to balance Medihub's pilot-to-scale path with Redwood's need to amortize engineering/observability investments for Private deployments. High level:

- Volume ladder: tiered discounts tied to committed token bands (quarterly true-ups). Example bands below.
- Platform fee phasing: spread the annual platform fee over a 12–24 month ramp for pilots converting to committed volumes.
- SLA carve-outs: tighter SLAs for core inference paths, with SLO exceptions during major upgrades/migrations.

Attached: quick SOW v1 and a support-tier matrix. Can you confirm: 1) expected first-year average peak TPS per region; 2) whether Medihub requires air-gapped delivery or VPC-only (we flagged both paths yesterday).

I'll follow up with suggested discount bands in a second email after Ben and Marissa weigh in.

Thanks —
Camila

Camila —

Appreciate the summary and the files. A few clarifying Qs from procurement and infra: 

1) Token bands — can you map these to our projected monthly calls? (we run two different models: triage and long-form summarization; they'd map to different token footprints).
2) Platform fee phasing — what's the downside if we ask for a 24-month deferral on the platform fee while we validate the pilot? Any material contract language we should expect?
3) SLA carve-outs — we need a firm fallback for our production inference (99.9 target). Can you give an example of the specific exceptions you mentioned?

Procurement also asked for an initial commercial term sheet (one page) they can share with legal. Can you send that?

Best,

Camila — quick thoughts:

Thanks for loop — I sketched concrete numbers that usually land for customers of this profile. If Medihub can commit to a minimum annual token commitment we can push deeper discounts and a capped platform fee ramp. Proposal (starter):

- Commitment bands (annual committed tokens, approximate):
  - Band A: 0–25M tokens — list pricing, platform fee waived for pilot months 1–3
  - Band B: 25–125M tokens — 12% discount off list; platform fee amortized over 18 months
  - Band C: 125–500M tokens — 18% discount; platform fee amortized over 12 months + one-time migration credit
  - Band D: 500M+ tokens — bespoke pricing (we typically move to seat/node blended SKU)

- SLA exceptions: planned maintenance windows and major model architecture change rollouts are carved out; critical inference path (user-facing calls) still kept at 99.9, fallback to hosted endpoint is mandatory as part of the runbook.

- Contract language: the main ask from procurement is clear true-up cadence and an exit protection clause for pilot failures.

I can convert this to a one-page commercial term sheet. Recommend offering a 10% pilot conversion credit if they move from pilot to Band B within 6 months.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Commercial Sales | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Medihub – volume ladder, platform fee phasing & SLA carve-outs

Sara / team —

Thanks for the questions. Attached is a concise commercial term sheet + an updated SOW with the platform fee phasing and explicit true-up cadence. Key points:

- We modeled two sample usage mixes (triage-heavy vs. long-form-heavy) in the term sheet to map to the token bands Ben suggested. That should make it easier for Procurement to see which band is closest to Medihub's forecast.
- Platform fee deferral: we can support a 24-month phasing but will require a minimum Band B annual commit to make it effective. If you opt for 24 months with a low commit, we will need a higher initial platform fee or a smaller discount.
- SLA carve-outs (examples included): major infrastructure upgrades (we give 7 days' notice), third-party hardware failures, and customer-side networking changes. For production inference we keep 99.9 (monthly), with an agreed on-call rotation and documented fallback to our hosted region — detailed in the SOW runbook.

Next steps: 1) tell me which of the sample usage mixes maps closest to your forecast, 2) confirm whether Medihub wants the 12- or 24-month platform fee phasing, and 3) I'll push the one-pager to legal after your procurement thumbs-up.

Camila

Attachments: Medihub_SOW_v1.pdf (updated), commercial-term-sheet-onepager.pdf (stub)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 13 Oct 2025 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Medihub term sheet — risk flags & approval level

Camila — internal note (please keep in thread for audit):

I reviewed Ben's bands and the draft term sheet. Two operational risk flags:

1) 24-month deferral increases exposure if they don't convert — require a 6–9 month conversion milestone tied to credits.
2) SLA fallback to hosted endpoints is fine, but Legal will want a clear indemnity carve-out and uptime measurement methods (rolling window vs. calendar month).

Recommendation: we can sign off on offering the 24-month phasing if Procurement accepts a conversion milestone (target: conversion to Band B within 9 months) and we log an acceptance signature on the runbook. Also recommend a 10% pilot-to-contract conversion credit (as Ben suggested) but capped at $100k.

I'll be available if legal has questions — happy to join the call.

—Marissa
VP, Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
